<root><h level="3" i="1">===HeartGold and SoulSilver===</h>
The following tutor moves are available in <template><title>game</title><part><name index="1"/><value>HeartGold and SoulSilver</value></part><part><name index="2"/><value>s</value></part></template>. Similar to Emerald, most of the moves that a Move Tutor can teach to a Pokémon require a set amount of Battle Points, these tutors being located in the [[Frontier Access]]. Fourteen of these moves are exclusive to HeartGold and SoulSilver, while the rest are also obtainable in Platinum.

<root><h level="2" i="1">==Trivia==</h>
* In Pokémon Platinum, there are exactly two [[shard]]-dependant tutorable moves for every type except <template><title>t</title><part><name index="1"/><value>Normal</value></part></template>, which has six.
* All of the tutorable moves in <template><title>2v2</title><part><name index="1"/><value>FireRed</value></part><part><name index="2"/><value>LeafGreen</value></part></template> (with the exception of the three moves taught at [[Cape Brink]]) were previously teachable via TM in [[Generation I]]. Similarly, all of the tutorable moves in <template><title>game</title><part><name index="1"/><value>Emerald</value></part></template> and <template><title>Pokémon XD</title></template> (with the exception of the moves that can only be taught to <template><title>p</title><part><name index="1"/><value>Mew</value></part></template>) were previously teachable via TM in [[Generation I]] and/or [[Generation II]].
* All of the free Move Tutors in Sword and Shield became TMs in Scarlet and Violet.
** Upon doing so, <template><title>p</title><part><name index="1"/><value>Mew</value></part></template> can learn all of them from the TMs, when it couldn't from the tutors.</root>

<root><h level="2" i="1">==Generation II==</h>
<h level="3" i="2">===Crystal===</h>
[[File:Move tutor.png|150px|right|thumb]]
In <template><title>game</title><part><name index="1"/><value>Crystal</value></part></template>, [[Bill]]'s father can be visited outside the [[Goldenrod Game Corner]] every Wednesday and Saturday if the player has the [[Coin Case]] and has entered the [[Hall of Fame]]. He teaches three different moves for 4000 coins, two of which were [[TM]]s in [[Generation I]] and returned to that status in [[Generation III]], and one of which later became a TM with the other two. These moves are breedable in the same fashion as TMs and HMs. After teaching a move, he goes back inside the Game Corner to gamble while nursing a drink, and will not be able to teach another move until the next available day.

The Move Tutor's son, Bill, complains that he doesn't work and is a drain on the family. His wife describes him as a former <template><title>tc</title><part><name index="1"/><value>Poké Maniac</value></part></template> who spends all his free time gambling.
